questions.question: Explain the difference between continuous training and interval training in endurance development. / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the difference between continuous training and interval training in endurance
  • development.
  • • Continuous training is performed at a steady pace without rest, while interval training
  • includes periods of exercise alternated with rest or recovery.
  • • Continuous training mainly develops aerobic endurance, whereas interval training
  • improves both aerobic and anaerobic endurance.
  • • In continuous training, the intensity remains constant, but interval training uses varying
  • intensities from high to low.
  • • Examples of continuous training are jogging and cycling, while interval training
  • includes sprints and HIIT workouts.
  • • Continuous training builds stamina over longer durations, while interval training
  • improves speed, power, and recovery ability more quickly.

questions.question: Examine the relationship between flexibility and injury prevention in sports training / [CO3] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the relationship between flexibility and injury prevention in sports training
  • • Flexibility improves range of motion and helps athletes perform movements efficiently
  • without putting excessive strain on muscles and joints.
  • • Good flexibility reduces muscle tightness and stiffness, lowering the chances of muscle
  • strains and cramps during sports activities.
  • • Proper flexibility supports correct body mechanics and posture, which helps prevent
  • overuse injuries and stress on joints.
  • • Dynamic stretching before exercise prepares muscles for activity and can reduce the risk
  • of injuries during performance.
  • • Excessive flexibility without strength can be harmful, as it may cause joint instability
  • and increase injury risk.
  • • Flexibility alone cannot prevent injuries; strength training, proper technique, rest, and
  • conditioning are also important factors.
  • • Different sports require different levels of flexibility, so athletes should focus on sport-
  • specific mobility and stretching exercises.
  • [5x4=20]

questions.question: Why is ethical behaviour important in fitness training?
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: Ethical behaviour is crucial in fitness training for several reasons:
  • Building Trust
  • Client-professional relationship: Trust is essential for a successful trainer -client relationship.
  • Ethical behaviour helps establish and maintain this trust.
  • Client safety: Trainers have a responsibility to ensure clients' safety and wellbeing.
  • Professional Integrity
  • Reputation: Ethical behaviour enhances a trainer's professional reputation and credibility.
  • Industry standards: Adhering to ethical standards contributes to the overall integrity of the
  • fitness industry.
  • Client Well-being Informed decision-making: Ethical trainers provide accurate information,
  • enabling clients to make informed decisions about their fitness journey.
  • Respect for clients' autonomy: Trainers should respect clients' boundaries, goals, and values.
  • ∙ Accountability Professional accountability: Ethical trainers are accountable for their actions
  • and decisions.
  • Continuous learning: Ethical trainers stay up -to-date with industry developments and best
  • practices.
  • ∙ Key Ethical Principles Respect for clients: Treat clients with dignity and respect.
  • Informed consent: Obtain clients' consent before starting a training program.
  • Confidentiality: Maintain clients' confidentiality and protect their personal information.
  • Professional boundaries: Establish and maintain appropriate boundaries with clients.
  • By prioritizing ethical behaviour, fitness trainers can build trust, maintain professional integrity,
  • and prioritize client well-being.

questions.question: Classify the basic principles of resistance training?
questions.solution_html:
• Answer: Here are the basic principles of resistance training:
  • ∙ Key Principles Overload: Gradually increase weight, resistance, or reps to challenge muscles.
  • Progression: Gradually increase intensity over time to continue making gains.
  • Specificity: Train specific muscle groups or movements to achieve desired adaptations.
  • Recovery: Allow adequate time for rest and recovery between workouts.
  • Variety: Incorporate different exercises, rep ranges, and training modalities.
  • Additional Considerations Individuality: Tailor training programs to individual needs, goals,
  • and fitness levels.
  • Periodization: Alternate training phases to avoid plateaus and prevent overtraining.
  • By applying these principles, individuals can design effective resistance training programs that
  • promote strength, muscle growth, and overall fitness.

  • not overly fatigued.
  • Better engagement: When participants are not exhausted, they're more likely to stay engaged
  • and motivated.

  • participants' well-being and comfort.

  • ∙ Modifications and Adjustments Adjusting intensity: Instructors can adjust intensity or
  • provide modifications to accommodate varying fatigue levels.

  • fatigue.
